title: Restricted Goldbach Sums over Arithmetic Progressions: A Corrected and Unified Treatment, with Ternary, Quaternary, and Conditional Extensions
content:
We give a unified, corrected, and self-contained treatment of the restricted weighted Goldbach sum \( R_{a,q}(N) := \sum_{\substack{p_1+p_2=N \\ p_1 \equiv a \ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)}} \left({\log{p}}_{1}\right)\left({\log{p}}_{2}\right),\ q\geq 1,\gcd{\left(a,q\right)}=1 \),
for moduli \( q=2^{k} \), \( 1≤k≤6 \). This edition merges two earlier documents from the same project: an August 2026 revision (internally “1Q”) that re-audited eleven prior drafts and closed the major-arc evaluation for growing moduli unconditionally whenever the Landau–Page exceptional modulus satisfies \( k_{1}(X)\leq logX \); and an extended treatise, subsequently published as [36], that develops structural rigidity results for the exceptional set, a sub-exponential exceptional-set bound, a ternary extension \( W_{a,q}(n) \), a restricted quaternary singular series, and a conditional hierarchy under the Density Hypothesis and GRH. The unification identified and removed one genuine mathematical error carried over from the unconditional core of [36]: an “almost-all” theorem asserting a fixed constant \( K≤38.92 \), built on an algebraically impossible optimisation step, which is precisely the error the 1Q audit had already identified and rejected in an earlier internal draft. That theorem is replaced here by the corrected effective almost-all theorem, whose threshold is an explicit function of X rather than a fixed constant, together with a theorem proving that no fixed constant can play that role. The unconditional core is proved for \( q=2^{k} \) only, since other moduli admit a genuine local obstruction that invalidates the main-term formula; this restriction, absent from the original statement of the rigidity and ternary results in [36], is now made explicit and those results are restated and re-derived accordingly. No Generalised Riemann Hypothesis or other unproved hypothesis is used anywhere in the unconditional core (Sections 3–12); GRH and the Density Hypothesis are used only in the clearly separated conditional appendix.
